title: DA3408 A4 · CPU Image Captioning — Observability
description: Streamlit BLIP captioning app instrumented with prometheus_client + node_exporter

panels.title: How to read this dashboard

options.content:
Top → bottom goes from **high-level health** to **low-level resources**: ① is everything up? → ② how much work is flowing? → ③ how fast is it? → ④ what are users sending? → ⑤ does app load explain the hardware load? → ⑥ raw node_exporter metrics.  
Colours are the colour-blind-safe **Okabe–Ito** palette. In every chart **single = blue, solid line** and **bulk = orange, dashed line**, with point markers on, so series stay distinguishable in greyscale print / PDF. Hover the ⓘ on any panel for its story.

panels.title: ① Service health — is everything up?
App status
panels.description: Is Prometheus able to scrape the Streamlit app's /metrics endpoint (:18000)? DOWN means the app process is dead or unreachable.

panels.title: node_exporter status
panels.description: Is the system-metrics exporter (:9100) being scraped? Without it, rows ⑤ and ⑥ go blank.

panels.title: Model
panels.description: 1 once the BLIP captioning model has been loaded into memory by the app.

panels.title: Images captioned
panels.description: Successful captions (single + bulk) within the selected time range.

panels.title: Failure rate
panels.description: Share of images that failed (corrupt files, decode errors, model errors) within the selected time range.

panels.title: Firing alerts
panels.description: Number of Prometheus alerting rules currently firing (see table below for which ones).

panels.title: Active requests
panels.description: Requests being processed right now (Gauge.track_inprogress), single + bulk.

panels.title: Bulk queue
panels.description: Images still waiting inside running ZIP jobs.

panels.title: App uptime
panels.description: Time since the Streamlit process started.

panels.title: App memory (RSS)
panels.description: Resident memory of the app process — mostly the model weights.

panels.title: Model load time
panels.description: How long the model took to load at startup (cold-start cost).

panels.title: Browser sessions
panels.description: Distinct Streamlit browser sessions opened since the app started.

panels.title: Firing alerts — Prometheus rules currently active
panels.description: Alerts from prometheus/rules.yml that are firing now; they are also routed to Alertmanager (:9093). Empty table = all good.

panels.title: ② Traffic & throughput — how much work is flowing?
Throughput · images captioned per second, by mode
panels.description: Rate of successful captions over a 30 s window. Bulk ZIP jobs show up as a sustained orange plateau; single uploads as short blue blips.

panels.title: Requests · uploads per minute, by mode
panels.description: Number of caption requests (button presses) in the last minute. One bulk request can contain up to 200 images.

panels.title: Requests by client · IP and session (custom labels)
panels.description: Total requests per client IP and Streamlit session id — the custom labels on caption_requests_total. Open the app in two tabs to see two sessions.

panels.title: Upload volume · bytes received per second, by mode
panels.description: Bytes uploaded by users (image or ZIP size). Large ZIPs appear as a single spike when the job starts.

panels.title: ③ Latency — how fast is each caption?
Inference latency percentiles · p50 / p90 / p99 per mode
panels.description: Per-image model time from the histogram caption_inference_seconds. Colour = percentile, dash = bulk. A widening p50→p99 gap means some images are much slower (large or detailed).

panels.title: Mean request time · summary vs histogram
panels.description: Mean end-to-end request time from the Summary caption_request_seconds (_sum/_count; includes the whole ZIP for bulk) next to mean per-image inference from the histogram.

panels.title: Latency distribution · images per latency bucket over time
panels.description: Each column is 30 s; darker/yellower cells = more images in that latency bucket. Uses the Cividis scale (colour-blind safe).

panels.title: Bulk job duration · mean time to finish one ZIP
panels.description: Mean wall-clock time per ZIP job (Summary caption_bulk_job_seconds), and the remaining queue. Longer jobs = bigger ZIPs or a slower CPU.

panels.title: ④ Inputs & outputs — what are users sending, what do they get?
Image size distribution · uploads per size bucket
panels.description: Histogram caption_image_bytes over the selected range: how many images fell at or below each file size.

panels.title: Caption length distribution · captions per word-count bucket
panels.description: Histogram caption_length_words: very short captions often indicate low-information images.

panels.title: ZIP entries skipped · by reason
panels.description: Files inside uploaded ZIPs that were ignored: not an image, larger than 10 MB, or beyond the 200-image limit.

panels.title: Errors · by mode and exception type
panels.description: Failures counted by caption_errors_total, labelled by mode and Python exception class (e.g. UnidentifiedImageError for corrupt files).

panels.title: ⑤ Application ↔ system correlation — does app load explain hardware load?
Throughput vs CPU · images/s (left) against node CPU busy % (right)
panels.description: When a bulk ZIP starts, the blue throughput area should rise together with the dashed vermillion CPU line — inference is CPU-bound.

panels.title: App memory vs node memory · app RSS (left) against node used % (right)
panels.description: App RSS jumps once when the model loads, then stays flat; node memory used % should track it. A steady climb would suggest a leak.

panels.title: In-flight work vs load · active requests + queue (left) against load avg (right)
panels.description: Pending work inside the app versus the OS 1-minute load average. Load rising while the queue drains confirms the app is the source of load.

panels.title: ⑥ System resources (node_exporter) — CPU, memory, disk, network
CPU utilisation · busy % by mode (stacked)
panels.description: Average across all cores. Model inference shows up as 'user' time; high 'iowait' would point to disk, high 'steal' to the VM host.

custom.axisLabel: CPU time (% of all cores) · linear

panels.title: Memory · used vs available vs cache
panels.description: Used = Total − Available. Cache/buffers are reclaimable, so 'available' is the number to watch.

panels.title: Disk usage · % of each filesystem used
panels.description: Space used per real filesystem (tmpfs/overlay excluded). Orange above 80 %, vermillion above 90 %.

panels.title: Disk I/O · bytes read vs written per second
panels.description: Summed over all disks. Reading a big ZIP or the model from disk shows as a read burst; steady writes are mostly Prometheus' own TSDB.

panels.title: Network · bytes received vs transmitted per second
panels.description: Summed over all interfaces except loopback. ZIP uploads from another machine appear as receive spikes.
